title: Smartphone PPG with ECG reference and acquisition disturbances
question: How do acquisition conditions affect pulse-signal quality and measurement error?
variables_and_units: Variables and units are preserved in native column headers, instrument metadata and source dictionaries; see evidence anchors below.
independent_units: Participant and complete recording; reference signals stay linked.
validation_design: Participant and complete recording; reference signals stay linked. Verify identifiers before allocating groups; the partition is not executed or frozen by this acquisition.
author_preprocessing: PPG was extracted from smartphone video; signals were manually synchronized and segmented by source authors. PPG 30 Hz, ECG 1,000 Hz, ACC 100 Hz per documentation. The package is not raw video.
prior_analysis_and_limits: The database was designed for PPG quality and heart-rate evaluation and has existing published analyses. Source quality flags mark some recordings unreliable; they are retained. Segments from a participant are strongly dependent; clinical deployment is outside acquisition acceptance. Read-only checks found 48 ECG and 48 PPG headers declaring a single frame with 10,000 or 300 channels, respectively; the other 3,840 recordings use conventional multiframe layouts. Header/data byte lengths and all 27,125 publisher-listed member hashes match. Preserve this source orientation difference. BUT smartphone PPG/WFDB and annotations; processed/reference products have distinct roles. Supplemental audit found 96 source headers with many declared channels and only one sample (48 ECG and 48 PPG). These are explicit layout anomalies; preserve them, do not silently transpose, and bound physiological inference to interpretable records unless the source convention is verified.
missingness: Native blanks, sentinels, absent records and source quality flags are preserved. No imputation performed by the curator. Exact missingness semantics come from source dictionaries/headers; no universal missing-value rule is imposed.
calibration: Use the retained source calibration files/standards and instrument metadata where provided. Absence of an explicit calibration record is not replaced by an assumed calibration.

eligibility.novelty: no unseen-law guarantee; independent adjudication required

exposure: Open source-aware; source literature and supplied analyses accessible
unit_interpretation: Use exact source field/sheet/channel labels and units in source_evidence and per-file reports; unknown units remain unresolved, not inferred from a variable name.
